scope.purpose: A small public-source seed for general prompt design, programming/debugging, evaluation, retrieval, factuality, risk, and provenance reasoning.

bounds.content_policy: Store concise paraphrases and short evidence excerpts, not full-page copies.
excluded_content: Provider API instructions that depend on current capabilities
Search snippets treated as factual evidence

project_fit.markdown_ingest: The project README describes Knowledge intake for pasted text and TXT/Markdown files; this report is intended to be the human-readable seed. The JSON is a provenance and graph manifest.
project_fit.initial_state: Keep sources local-only. Any Campus indexing or egress requires the project's explicit permission and budget flow.
project_fit.not_claimed: This research does not establish that ingestion, graph extraction, retrieval, or answer grounding works in the application.

research_method.retrieval_mode: Public page fetches parsed with --md; source pages were read directly, not inferred from snippets.
research_method.search_status: A Google Search request returned a CAPTCHA, so no Google Search is claimed or used as evidence. Bing RSS searches were noisy/mismatched and were not used to substantiate claims.
research_method.provider_calls: None. No inference API, credentials, private source, or bulk scraping was used.
limitations: Live documentation may change; timestamps identify the inspected snapshot.
The two OpenAI pages include near-term platform/API deprecation notices. Only general prompt and evaluation methods are proposed for reuse.
The RAG paper reports results for its own models, baselines, and datasets; those findings are not a universal performance guarantee.

chunks.summary: OpenAI's guide treats prompts as application artifacts that should be maintained and reviewed with product changes. It explicitly recommends running prompt tests and evaluation cases when publishing. The generic takeaway is to version prompt changes and check them against representative cases; provider-specific message placement and prompt-object APIs are not generalized.
chunks.evidence_excerpt: Run your prompt tests and evaluation cases every time you publish.
chunks.source_section: Refine your prompt; Prompts in your application

chunks.summary: Google's Gemini guide recommends clear, specific instructions and distinguishes question, task, entity, and partial-completion inputs. This taxonomy can help a prompt writer state what the input represents and what operation is requested. The source is Gemini-specific; this chunk does not endorse Gemini syntax or capability.
chunks.evidence_excerpt: provide it with clear and specific instructions.

chunks.summary: The guide describes an evaluation loop: specify the task and criteria, run test inputs, inspect results, then iterate. This is a provider-neutral evaluation pattern. The guide's API examples and platform lifecycle are time-sensitive and should not be treated as current implementation instructions.
chunks.evidence_excerpt: Analyze the results, then iterate and improve on your prompt.

chunks.summary: The paper defines RAG models as combining parametric memory in a pretrained sequence-to-sequence model with non-parametric memory in a dense vector index, accessed by a pretrained neural retriever. In this study, generation is conditioned on retrieved passages as well as the input.
chunks.evidence_excerpt: models which combine pre-trained parametric and non-parametric memory for language generation.

chunks.summary: The paper reports state-of-the-art results on three open-domain question-answering tasks and more specific, diverse, factual language than a parametric-only baseline. These are findings for the paper's models, tasks, datasets, and comparison; they are not a guarantee that every RAG implementation improves factuality.
chunks.evidence_excerpt: more specific, diverse and factual language than a state-of-the-art parametric-only seq2seq baseline.

chunks.topic: AI risk management across a lifecycle
chunks.summary: NIST describes AI RMF as voluntary and intended to incorporate trustworthiness considerations into AI system design, development, use, and evaluation. Its landing page said AI RMF 1.0 was being revised at access time, so version-specific recommendations need a fresh source check.
chunks.evidence_excerpt: incorporate trustworthiness considerations into the design, development, use, and evaluation of AI products, services, and systems.

chunks.summary: OWASP distinguishes direct injection from indirect injection carried in external content such as websites or files. It says RAG and fine-tuning do not fully mitigate prompt injection. Derived design implication: retrieved passages should be treated as untrusted data and their instructions should not gain authority merely because retrieval returned them.
chunks.evidence_excerpt: research shows that they do not fully mitigate prompt injection vulnerabilities.
chunks.source_section: Overview; Types of Prompt Injection Vulnerabilities

chunks.summary: MDN recommends validating code before investigating specific errors, then using browser developer tools and console output to locate problems. Its lesson distinguishes syntax and logic errors and covers conditionals, try/catch, and throw for handling errors. This chunk is JavaScript-specific.
chunks.evidence_excerpt: You should validate your code first before trying to track down specific errors.
chunks.source_section: Recap on types of JavaScript error; Linting your code

chunks.summary: Google SRE says testing can demonstrate equivalence on changed paths and reduce uncertainty, with needed coverage depending on reliability requirements. It also states that passing tests do not necessarily prove reliability. Test results should therefore be reported with their scope and combined with relevant operational evidence.
chunks.evidence_excerpt: Passing a test or a series of tests doesn’t necessarily prove reliability.
chunks.source_section: Testing for Reliability; Relationships Between Testing and Mean Time to Repair

chunks.summary: PROV-O expresses a provenance data model using interoperable classes and properties. Its starting terms define an Entity as a thing with fixed aspects, an Activity as something that occurs over time and acts on or uses entities, and an Agent as something responsible for an activity or entity. A PromptLab mapping can represent a source as an Entity, ingestion/build as an Activity, and publisher/reviewer as an Agent.
chunks.evidence_excerpt: An Activity is something that occurs over a period of time and acts upon or with entities.

proposed_ingestion_and_verification_acce: Keep this corpus bounded to the 9 listed sources and 10 chunks; keep each chunk under 140 words and do not ingest whole pages.
For every chunk, preserve source ID, URL, access timestamp, section, and evidence excerpt; confirm each excerpt against the source page.
Review every graph edge against its listed evidence chunk. Keep study findings and application mappings labeled; remove any edge without direct textual support or an explicitly labeled mapping.

Do not convert provider-specific API migration notices, model names, capabilities, or reasoning-effort choices into general advice. Recheck current official capability documentation before making such recommendations.
Use the Markdown report for project Knowledge intake; retain JSON as the structured provenance/graph manifest. The README says JSON is not among the listed upload types.
Start in local-only state. Do not grant Campus indexing or trigger provider egress without the project's explicit consent and budget flow.

Prepare 12 fixed retrieval-preview questions spanning prompt design, programming/debugging, evaluation, RAG, prompt injection, risk management, reliability, and provenance. Require an expected chunk in the top five for each query and visible source attribution for each retrieved chunk.
Manually verify every factual answer against its cited chunk and source. If the corpus has no supporting chunk, label the topic as uncovered instead of filling the gap with an uncited claim.
Record actual ingest/build/retrieval results separately. This research manifest alone is not evidence that GraphRAG works.
